Once again VERY nice and useful analytics!

Disciplines:
Perhaps the inclusion of some not so stellar disciplines like Celerity is to the fact that they are a support disciplines which are found in the Vampires but not really used in the decks?

Or does the data you've used only count the single most used discipline in each deck or, better yet, estimate from the Library contents what is the main discipline of each of the decks?

Achetypes:
-I haven't run across the term Guns 'n' Roses before but thought it was extremely descriptive and funny to boot!
-What is a "killer" deck? ("stealth killer", "big cap killer")
-Great to see Gangrel perform well EXPECIALLY with having Stanislava decks separated from them!

I wonder if there would be a way to somehow include the tournament size to these findings?
Although, first we'd need to define what makes a small, medium or large tournament.
Although, a problem that would rise from this is the fact that there aren't really all that many larger, or even medium, tournaments being held... :/

But perhaps doing an annual data gathering for only larger (or larger AND medium) tournaments might be attainable?

Hi! Thanks for reading and for your comments!

About disciplines, at the moment the feature is counting decks that include at least 1 card of a given discipline. Due to the nature of my research, I could not think of an easy way to count discipline cards in each deck (what would be the most precise). It requires a lot of time and is beyond my possibilities right now...

I like to think on the disciplines chart as an indicator... there are other features that are much more precise.

I was surprised too by the high rate of Cel, but I think it has to do with the good rates for Banu Haqim, Brujah and Toreador guns (or Guns´n´Roses hehe). I believe we use to think on Cel as a support discipline, but maybe after V5 we should rethink that... I will remember to follow up this on the next months...

The killer denomination, I though it would reflect they are decks that are focused on direct attack to the pool of their prey. I tried to illustrate their aggressive mood, but it is just a personal denomination, and I´m open to suggestions

Yeah, Stanislava won just 1 of the 9 tournament won by Gangrel. Not good times for her, it seems

And regarding tournament size, I am already considering the number of players in the events as a % rate for most indicators, but I agree with you in the need to discriminate big events from regular ones. I am thinking of a max number of players to include the event in the regular season... 50 or 75 is what now I am thinking of, and maybe 50 is the best number. What are your thoughts?

Annual summary of big events is a very good idea... I find they have their own, different meta. I will write it in my calendar! Thanks!

Hello! I agree with you that Ashur tablets and multimaster, being a good sinergy, are somehow reducing their impact. According to my counting, they have lowered their rate of success from 25% to 20% in the last few months. This may be due to the fast meta, or maybe to their auto-correction condition (the more ashur tablets are seen in a tournament, the harder it is to get a good revenue from them).

Emerald Legionnaires, on the other side, are growing in importance, and the Emerald Harbinger archetype has been quite successful in Q2. I am working on the consolidated data for the spring season, and they have become one of the 5 most successful arquetypes. I don´t see a problem with that, anyway. They are a solid archetype and deserve to be there, but their succcess is by no means abusive. In fact, there is no archetype that can be called a "bully" so far this year.

Decks that use Emerald Legionnaires outside of the Harbinger clan are rare these days, though they are still very good. This year, I can think on the one piloted by Tomas Lopez in the finals in the Spanish NC

(

)

Also, maybe they get some more love, now that BCN Crisis has made a video about his brilliant version

(

)

But I believe there may be some issue with them as long as, like you say, probably more people are learning how to play against them. Good point!
